intent: Canonical sort. Must call view.grid.sort(['activity'], [false]). Must NOT assign to view.grid.sortByColumns (getter-only, silent no-op). Must NOT reference a `grokky` global (does not exist in datagrok-exec).

Display-only hide. The row-header column in Datagrok has an empty-string name (''), is at grid index 0, and may also be referenced as '#' or 'index' in user vocabulary. Any of: grid.col('').visible=false, grid.columns.byIndex(0).visible=false, grid.col('index'/'#').visible=false, or grid.columns.setVisible([...]) is acceptable. Must NOT remove the column from the DataFrame.

prompt: Pin the SMILES column to the left
intent: Built-in pin via gridCol.pin() (left-only). view.grid.col('SMILES').pin() is canonical. PowerGrid plugin path is heavier than needed.

prompt: Make the molecule column 300 pixels wide
intent: view.grid.col('molecule').width = 300. Single-column pixel width; the width policy APIs cover all columns at once and would be wrong here.

prompt: Color-code the activity column from red to green
intent: Data-side linear color coding via col.meta.colors.setLinear([...]). Grid-only color paths (gridCol.backColor, categoryColors) would NOT propagate to other viewers and are wrong for 'color-code the column'. Manually setting color-coding tags via setTag is also wrong — use the meta.colors helpers.

prompt: Set the format of IC50 to 2 decimal places
intent: col.meta.format = '0.00' is canonical. gridCol.format = '0.00' is the grid-only override and also passes; either path is acceptable.

prompt: Show only these columns: SMILES, MW, LogP, activity
intent: Bulk show-only via grid.columns.setVisible(['SMILES', 'MW', 'LogP', 'activity']). Toggling each gridCol.visible per name plus per-name hides is acceptable but verbose.
view.grid.sort([], []) clears the grid sort without touching anything else. Must NOT call view.resetLayout() (which closes every viewer the user added).
Restore visibility for every column. A for-loop over grid.columns from index 1 setting visible=true is canonical (index 0 is the row header). resetLayout is too blunt — closes viewers.

prompt: Turn off color coding on the activity column
intent: col.meta.colors.setDisabled(). Must target the activity column specifically, not all columns (that's a full reset).

prompt: Pin SMILES on the left, hide the index column, color activity red-to-green, sort by activity desc
intent: Headline multi-step recipe. Four operations in one block: pin SMILES, hide index, linear color on activity (red->green), sort activity desc. Order is flexible — coloring is data-side and independent of grid-side.

prompt: Reset the grid customization but keep my viewers
intent: Composed reset: restore visibility, reset width policy (Optimal), clear sort, disable per-column color coding. Must NOT call view.resetLayout() — that closes scatter plots / histograms / filter panels the user added.

prompt: Sort by class ascending, then activity descending
intent: Multi-column sort with parallel booleans: grid.sort(['class', 'activity'], [true, false]). Single call.

User suggests the wrong API. Claude must NOT comply — sortByColumns is getter-only and assignment is a silent no-op. Correct path: view.grid.sort(['activity'], [false]). Pass if Claude ignores the framing or explicitly explains why sortByColumns is wrong.
notes: The forbidden_symbols check is the primary gate. Bonus if Claude calls out the trap in prose.

prompt: Rename the activity column in the grid display to 'Potency'
intent: User asks for grid-display rename. gridCol.name = 'Potency' would rename the underlying DF column (destructive — breaks every reference). Correct: col.meta.friendlyName = 'Potency'. The skill explicitly traps this.
notes: friendlyName lives in df-and-columns conceptually but the col.meta.friendlyName setter is part of the raw API.

prompt: Reset the layout to just the grid
intent: Ambiguous: 'reset the layout to just the grid' literally maps to view.resetLayout() (closes viewers AND resets the grid), but a user might mean reset the grid alone. Pass if Claude (a) picks view.resetLayout() as the natural interpretation, (b) composes a manual reset, or (c) surfaces the distinction in prose before picking.
notes: Intentionally hard. Any reasonable resolution passes; only a silent no-op or unrelated tool fails.

prompt: Reset all grid customization back to default
intent: Composed reset: clear sort, restore visibility, set width policy back to Optimal, disable per-column color coding. resetLayout is wrong — it ALSO closes viewers.

prompt: Reset all grid customization — clear the sort, restore all hidden columns, reset widths, and turn off color coding
intent: Composed reset across all four dimensions, OR view.resetLayout(). Forbidden: closing views / tables — the user wants the grid presentation reset, not the workspace blown away.
notes: Sharpened from earlier ambiguous 'clear everything' — that wording let Claude reach for grok.shell.closeAll.
